lead: Ann Arbor plumbing deals with cold winters, older homes near downtown and basements. PipeMend sends licensed local plumbers across Ann Arbor.
risk: frozen pipes, aging pipes in older homes and basement backups
risk_short: frozen pipes, old pipes and basements
why: The Old West Side, Burns Park and Kerrytown have homes from the 1870s to the 1930s with galvanized supply lines, cast-iron stacks and clay sewer laterals. Many near campus are rentals.
Winters freeze pipes near exterior walls. Heavy rain backs water into basements, and the city has a footing drain disconnection program in some areas.
utility: City of Ann Arbor Water Treatment Services
water: Ann Arbor treats water mainly from the Huron River, plus wells, and softens it at the plant. It is moderately hard after treatment.
problems: Old West Side and Burns Park
tips: Keep the heat on and cabinets open in deep cold.
Test your sump pump each spring.
Scope the sewer line before buying an older home.
Give tenants a shutoff valve map.
areas: PipeMend works in the Old West Side, Burns Park, Kerrytown, Water Hill, Ann Arbor Hills, the North Side and every other Ann Arbor neighborhood.
permits: Plumbing permits come from the City of Ann Arbor Building Services, and plumbers must be licensed by Michigan LARA.

faq.a: Yes. The city softens Huron River water at its treatment plant, so it is moderately hard at the tap. Some homes still add a softener for extra protection.
